tasks.title: Tests for a leap year
tasks.statement: Complete the class TestLeap (unittest): tests for the function is_leap(year). The checker runs your tests against a correct implementation (they must PASS) and against three broken ones (they must FAIL). Cover a typical year, century years, and years divisible by 400.

tasks.title: Tests for clamp
tasks.statement: Complete the class TestClamp: tests for the function clamp(x, low, high), which limits x to the range [low, high]. Your tests must pass on the correct implementation and fail on each of the three broken ones. Check values inside, below, above, and on the boundaries.
tasks.hint: clamp(5, 0, 10) == 5; clamp(-3, 0, 10) == 0; clamp(42, 0, 10) == 10; and the boundaries themselves.

tasks.title: Tests for divide
tasks.statement: Complete the class TestDivide: tests for the function divide(a, b), which is ordinary division and must raise ValueError when b == 0. Your tests must pass on the correct implementation and fail on three broken ones. Don't forget assertRaises.

tasks.title: Tests for fizzbuzz
tasks.statement: Complete the class TestFizz: tests for the function fizzbuzz(n), which returns «FizzBuzz» for multiples of 15, «Fizz» for multiples of 3, «Buzz» for multiples of 5, and otherwise the number as a string. Your tests must pass on the correct implementation and fail on three broken ones.
tasks.hint: assertEqual(fizzbuzz(15), "FizzBuzz"), 9, 5, 10 (for Buzz, both an odd and an even multiple), 7 → "7".

tasks.title: Tests for a stack
tasks.statement: Complete the class TestStack: tests for the class Stack with the methods push(x), pop() (removes the top item; on an empty stack it raises IndexError), peek() (the top item without removing it), and size(). The tests must pass on the correct implementation and fail on three broken ones.
tasks.hint: Push 1, 2, 3: pop() == 3, peek() == 2, size() == 2; on an empty stack: with self.assertRaises(IndexError): self.s.pop().

tasks.hint: >>> abs_diff(5, 8)\n    3: each example is a line with >>> and a line with the expected result.

tasks.title: Total through a client
tasks.statement: Write a function total_cost(client, items): the sum of the prices of all goods in the list items; the price of each one is returned by client.get_price(item). The client is passed as a parameter, so it can be replaced in a test.

tasks.title: Time as a parameter
tasks.statement: Write a function greeting(now), where now is a datetime object. Before 12 o'clock, return «Good morning»; from 12 to 18, «Good afternoon»; later, «Good evening». Do not call the current time inside.
